title: relationship event orchestration
question: Which people, identity, asset, contract, and evidence actions must complete when a worker transfers or a contractor engagement ends?
scenario: Clinical-to-procurement transfer: An employee moves departments and gains new purchasing duties while retaining a clinical role.
focalRelation: A relationship event triggers coordinated owner actions; a mover removes obsolete access before or with new access; a leaver or contractor end requires verified revocation across physical, logical, session, key, device, and supplier paths.

prediction.prompt: Which people, identity, asset, contract, and evidence actions must complete when a worker transfers or a contractor engagement ends?

options.label: Keep every old entitlement until the employee confirms the new role is comfortable.
options.feedback: That creates unmanaged privilege accumulation; retain only justified duties through explicit approval and time bounds.

options.label: Remove old access, grant approved new access, and verify every affected path.
options.feedback: A personnel or contract status change does not execute technical and physical revocation or prove asset return.

options.label: Updating the HR record automatically revokes every access path and session.
options.feedback: The event is a trigger; each identity, session, key, device, physical credential, and supplier account needs verified action.

prediction.hint: A role change requires both removal of old access and bounded approval of new access.

retry.prompt: A contractor’s engagement ends Friday, but the account is reviewed only monthly. Which change most directly reduces exposure?

options.label: An HR termination record automatically ends all access
options.feedback: Technical and physical access, sessions, keys, supplier accounts, and assets require coordinated revocation and verification.

options.label: The authoritative end event precedes the periodic review
options.feedback: Correct. The authoritative end event precedes the periodic review.

options.label: Keep every old entitlement until the employee confirms the new role is comfortable
options.feedback: That shortcut ignores the decisive changed fact. The authoritative end event precedes the periodic review.

retry.hint: Look for explicit reapproval, an end date, and reconciliation of every downstream entitlement.

takeaway: Use the case evidence to apply this relation: A relationship event triggers coordinated owner actions; a mover removes obsolete access before or with new access; a leaver or contractor end requires verified revocation across physical, logical, session, key, device, and supplier paths.
assumptions: Only entities and claims anchored in the canonical unit or explicitly labeled hypothetical scenario are used.
A highlighted path means the learner is inspecting that path; it does not assert the event occurred.
The current source is authoritative for facts; this treatment reorganizes presentation without changing canonical content.
The lesson teaches one bounded decision and does not claim to exhaust every jurisdiction, vendor implementation, architecture, attack, or exception.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The timeline preserves the authoritative mover event, sponsor decision, old-access removal, approved new access, asset and facility actions, completion evidence, and a time-bounded retained clinical duty. It does not render separate joiner, mover, leaver, and contractor swimlanes or a proportionality inset.

learningJob.plainExplanation: A role change must trigger explicit sponsor decisions, access changes, asset transfers, and completion evidence. A temporary retained duty needs separate approval and an expiry rather than blanket legacy access.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A lifecycle view adds value when all event, decision, action, and evidence columns remain visible; the current opening omits most of that model.
